name: U.S. Web Design System (USWDS)
vendor: U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Technology Transformation Services
licence: Public domain in the US + CC0 1.0 worldwide for GSA work; bundled third-party parts (e.g. Material Icons sprite, fonts) keep their own licences (Apache-2.0 / OFL) per LICENSE.md in @uswds/uswds 3.14.0
bestFor: government, public-sector, healthcare, education and any service where trust and accessibility outrank flair
content-heavy informational sites and transactional forms (memorable date, input mask, step indicator, validation)
teams that want a token architecture with hard guardrails: themes can only pick from system tokens
projects that need contrast guaranteed by construction (grade 'magic numbers')
avoidFor: brand-expressive SaaS marketing (deliberately plain; looks governmental)
dark-mode-first products (no global dark theme; only a usa-dark-background helper)
motion-rich or highly interactive app UIs (single 0.15s ease-in-out transition token)
teams that cannot run Sass (theme tokens are Sass settings compiled at build)

families: sans (ui, body): Source Sans Pro Web (default $theme-font-type-sans), cap-height 340px; Public Sans Web available (cap 362px, the base)
roles: ui=sans, heading=serif, body=sans, code=mono, alt=serif
typography.notes: Px values are DERIVED from the default settings via the normalize-type-scale() formula: rendered size = 362px (system base cap height) / typeface cap height x system size. So 16px in Source Sans renders 17.04px and 40px Merriweather renders 39.0px: every face is optically matched to Public Sans. Line-heights are also normalized (token / (362/cap), rounded to 0.1): body token 5 (1.62) -> 1.5 for Source Sans; heading token 2 (1.2) stays 1.2 for Merriweather. System type scale: micro 10, 1:12, 2:13, 3:14, 4:15, 5:16, 6:17, 7:18, 8:20, 9:22, 10:24, 11:28, 12:32, 13:36, 14:40, 15:48, 16:56, 17:64, 18:80, 19:120, 20:140. Line-height tokens 1:1, 2:1.2, 3:1.35, 4:1.5, 5:1.62, 6:1.75. Measure tokens 1-6 = 44/60/64/68/72/88ex (default body measure 4 = 68ex, narrow 1 = 44ex). Weights limited to light 300 / normal 400 / bold 700 by default. Root font size respects user setting (theme-respect-user-font-size: true).

color.model: hex, organised as HSL-hue families x luminance grades 5-90 (plus vivid 'v' variants); grade = relative-luminance band

neutrals.theme roles: base-lightest gray-5, base-lighter gray-cool-10, base-light gray-cool-30, base gray-cool-50, base-dark gray-cool-60, base-darker gray-cool-70, base-darkest/ink gray-90

accents.system families (24): red, red-warm, red-cool, orange, orange-warm, gold, yellow, green, green-warm, green-cool, mint, mint-cool, cyan, blue, blue-warm, blue-cool, indigo, indigo-warm, indigo-cool, violet, violet-warm, magenta, gray, gray-warm, gray-cool (+transparents)

color.darkMode: No global dark theme. Components can sit on dark via the usa-dark-background package and the reverse text colour token ($theme-text-reverse-color: white). Contrast on any background is computed from grades at build time, so 'dark mode' is achieved by choosing high-grade backgrounds, not by a token remap.
color.contrastNotes: Contrast is built into token names. 'Magic number' = grade difference: 40+ = AA large text (3:1), 50+ = AA (4.5:1) / AAA large, 70+ = AAA (7:1); grade 50 passes AA against both white (0) and black (100). Grade bands by relative luminance: 5: .85-.93, 10: .75-.82, 20: .50-.65, 30: .35-.45, 40: .225-.30, 50: .175-.183, 60: .10-.125, 70: .05-.07, 80: .02-.04, 90: .005-.015. Encoded in Sass as $system-wcag-magic-numbers (AA 50, AAA 70, AA-large 40) and checked at compile time. Measured: primary #005ea2 vs white 6.72:1; ink #1b1b1b vs white 17.22:1; base gray-cool-50 #71767a vs white 4.59:1 (grade 50 rule holds); secondary red-50 #d83933 4.61:1.

spacing.base: 8px ($system-spacing-grid-base) with half steps; units(n) = n x 8px
spacing.notes: Tokens: '1px','2px','05'=4,'1'=8,'105'=12,'2'=16,'205'=20,'3'=24,'4'=32,'5'=40,'6'=48,'7'=56,'8'=64,'9'=72,'10'=80,'15'=120, plus named large widths card 160, card-lg 240, mobile 320, mobile-lg 480, tablet 640, tablet-lg 880, desktop 1024, desktop-lg 1200, widescreen 1400 which double as breakpoints. Negative versions exist. Site margins 32px desktop / 16px mobile; column gaps 2px/16px/24px.

radius.rule: theme radius sm 2px, md 0.5 unit = 4px, lg 1 unit = 8px. Buttons use md (4px); cards lg (8px) with 2px base-lighter border.

depth.borders: Borders and fills carry most structure: card 2px base-lighter, alert 8px left bar (bar width 1 unit), button stroke 2px for outline variant. High-contrast-mode border colours tokenised separately.

motion.notes: u-transition(prop, easing, $essential) mixin removes the transition under prefers-reduced-motion unless the animation is flagged essential. No motion scale.

controlHeightsPx.button padding default: 12px x 20px (height depends on line-height; not tokenised)

components.stateMatrixCompleteness: Medium-high for forms (error, success, disabled, focus, hint, validation states per input; aria-disabled styles) but low for colour states as tokens (hover/active are picked as darker grades per component in Sass, not tokenised). Count = usa-* packages in @uswds/uswds 3.14.0 that are components (74 usa-* packages minus 29 typography/layout/helper packages such as usa-prose, usa-layout-grid, usa-dark-background, usa-hint).

tokenArchitecture: Two strict tiers plus settings. SYSTEM tokens: the complete closed vocabulary (24 colour families x grades 5-90 [+vivid], type scale 1-20, line-height 1-6, measure 1-6, spacing units, breakpoints, cap heights). THEME tokens: a small role-based subset set in Sass settings files that may ONLY reference system tokens ($theme-color-primary: 'blue-60v'; $theme-h1-font-size: '2xl'; $theme-border-radius-md: 0.5). Components consume theme tokens through functions/mixins (color(), units(), size(), radius()) and utility classes; raw values are rejected at compile time with an error. State tokens (error/warning/success/info/disabled/emergency) are themed families too. Theme token names are positional (lightest/lighter/light/base/vivid/dark/darker/darkest) so a project can swap 'blue' for 'green-cool' without touching components.
distinctiveness: Contrast-by-arithmetic: colour grades are luminance bands, so subtracting grade numbers tells you the WCAG level without a checker. Optical normalization of every typeface to a common cap height so font swaps never break the rhythm. A serif (Merriweather) heading voice over a sans body, rare in UI systems. Theme layer that physically cannot introduce off-system values.
weaknesses: No dark theme, no density modes, one transition token
Sass build step required for theming; CSS custom properties are not the primary API
Normalized sizes produce fractional px (17.04px body) which surprises designers working in Figma
takeaways: Encode contrast in colour names: grade = luminance band, so 'grade difference >= 50' guarantees 4.5:1 and >= 70 guarantees 7:1
Two-tier tokens with a hard rule: theme tokens may only point at system tokens, enforced at build
Normalize type sizes by typeface cap height (target 362px cap at 1000 UPM-equivalent) so swapping fonts keeps optical size and leading
Positional theme names (lighter/light/base/dark/darker/vivid) let a project re-hue the whole product by changing the family
Measure (line length) is a first-class token in ex units (44-88ex)
Reduced motion via a transition mixin with an explicit 'essential' flag
provenance: public-spec (@uswds/uswds@3.14.0 packages/uswds-core/src/styles tokens, settings, variables, functions; dist/css/uswds.min.css for shadows; designsystem.digital.gov color overview and design-tokens pages); type px values derived from the source formula; contrast ratios measured by computation
